rationale: The natural-timing probe bounded the interleaving at zero in 792 deliveries and pointed the open question at the width of the election's read-modify-write rather than at delivery density, since heavier delivery postpones the campaign it is trying to catch. This turn follows that direction with a probe that keeps natural timing but gives the term write a realistic slow-store latency: a store that sleeps before applying the current-term write, as a fsync on a busy disk does, is an environment property rather than a hook that holds one specific write open, and it widens the window to the store's write latency. Every heartbeat delivered during that latency is written inside the election's read-modify-write, so if the window width is what has kept the rate down, falls should appear here without any instrumentation of the write path. The reading rule is the same as before and was fixed in advance: a sampled term below the highest term already adopted is a monotonicity violation, and a count of such falls per delivery is the result, while a zero here together with the earlier zero would say the width is not what limits it and would send the question back to the delivery structure.

investigations.discriminator: Hold the main loop's term write open by supplying a stable store whose write of the current term can be armed to block once, deliver one empty heartbeat with a term well above the current one on the fast path while it is held, then release and read both the in-memory term and the persisted term: a term after release lower than the term adopted during the hold witnesses a durable term regression caused by the off-thread write. Executed twice with the same operands (d5d2d6e4b4304f65ba05d1865 and f5bfa53fce5c4314a29fe898c38b8808), the control with the same hold and no heartbeat (68ee55636577494e915fce091da4d876) shows the held write alone is monotone, and a natural-timing probe with no instrumentation saw zero falls in 792 deliveries (c839d00a425a4b75b09fbfb353fc4fc8). The open question is now whether the rate rises when the window is as wide as a slow durable write rather than a couple of instructions, which the queued probe tests with a store that sleeps before applying the current-term write and no hold-open hook.

knowledge.assertion: the candidate path reads the current term, computes the next one and writes it with no guard around the pair, so a higher term written off the main thread in between is overwritten in memory and in the stable store
with no instrumented store, no fall was observed in 792 fast-path deliveries followed by immediate term samples on a single-voter node

scope.description: Probe whether a slow durable term write raises the natural rate of the term-regression interleaving: on a real single-node cluster over a store that sleeps before applying the current-term write, deliver empty heartbeats on the fast path in a loop while sampling the term repeatedly after each delivery, and emit one CA_EVENT JSON line with the write latency, deliveries, failures, samples, falls, the first fall, the highest adopted term, and the final term, persisted term and state.
assumptions: A store that sleeps before the current-term write models a durable write on a busy disk; it slows every such write rather than holding one chosen write open, so the timing stays natural and only the window width changes.
The node is a single voter, so every election it starts resolves at once and any fall observed comes from the write ordering rather than from vote traffic.
A sampled term below the highest term already adopted is a monotonicity violation, since this implementation only ever writes the current term plus one or an adopted higher term.
The heartbeat that triggers the off-thread write comes from the harness wrapper that mirrors the network transport's classification and dispatch rather than the network transport itself.

experiment.prefix: The harness (draft/assurance_generated_test.go) is one TestAssurance-prefixed test plus two local helpers. It wraps an in-memory transport so strictly empty AppendEntries requests are dispatched to the installed handler on the caller's goroutine with a bounded response wait, and wraps the in-memory store so that a write of the current-term key sleeps three milliseconds before being applied, which is the write that sits inside the candidate path's read-modify-write. It bootstraps a single-voter configuration with BootstrapCluster and starts the node with NewRaft over those objects, waits (bounded) for Leader state, records the highest adopted term, then loops for eight seconds: it reads the node's term, delivers one empty heartbeat three terms above it, raises the highest adopted term when the node has moved up, counts a failure otherwise, and then samples the term six times in quick succession, counting a fall whenever a sample is below the highest adopted term and recording the first one with its operands. It finishes by printing one CA_EVENT JSON line with the write latency, delivery and sample counts, fall count, first fall and the final term, persisted term and state, then shuts the node down.
